question: What is the value of frac{{1 - {{tan }²}A}}{{1 + {{tan }²}A}}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the expression as a **standard trigonometric identity**.

The formula for **cos 2A** in terms of **tan A** is directly given by:

cos 2A = (1 − tan²A) / (1 + tan²A)

By comparing the given expression with the identity, we get the result **cos 2A**.

**∴ The correct answer is cos 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression is (1 − tan²A) / (1 + tan²A).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c24f7a9f540401e15957b58e9a556f89dfd1ad795a5c23f72d3d3458b5e10982.png] 

⇒ Substitute **tan A = sin A / cos A** into the expression:

⇒ Expression = [1 − (sin²A / cos²A)] / [1 + (sin²A / cos²A)]

⇒ Expression = [(cos²A − sin²A) / cos²A] / [(cos²A + sin²A) / cos²A]

⇒ Expression = (cos²A − sin²A) / (cos²A + sin²A)

⇒ We know the **Pythagorean identity**: cos²A + sin²A = 1

⇒ Expression = (cos²A − sin²A) / 1

⇒ Expression = **cos 2A** (Using the double angle identity for cosine)

**∴ The correct answer is cos 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sine Double Angle Identity

The value of **sin 2A** in terms of **tan A** is given by: 2 tan A / (1 + tan²A).

Tangent Double Angle Identity

The value of **tan 2A** in terms of **tan A** is given by: 2 tan A / (1 − tan²A).

Cosine Double Angle Variants

**cos 2A** can also be written as **cos²A − sin²A**, or **2cos²A − 1**, or **1 − 2sin²A**.

Secant Identity

The denominator 1 + tan²A is equivalent to **sec²A** according to the Pythagorean identity.</p
